column1: # DRAFT (not executed; see README.md). G1 phase 3: len and unique.
# len's argument is any integer-domain constraint (the count atom
# reuses the numeric algebra recursively); the domain — string length,
# list element count, map entry count — is fixed by the peer.
# String length is counted in UNICODE CODE POINTS — not UTF-16 code
# units (TS native) and not bytes (Go native). U+1D11E MUSICAL SYMBOL
# G CLEF is one code point, two UTF-16 units, four UTF-8 bytes.
# len emptiness reuses the numeric algebra: len(c) empty iff
# unique() compares whole elements by scalar identity — leaf AND
# value — so [1, 1.0] IS pairwise distinct under the tower.
# unique() applies to lists AND maps -- map ENTRY VALUES pairwise
# distinct, since keys are distinct by construction. Any other peer is
# a domain conflict. Uniqueness by PROJECTION ("no two services share a
# port") stays deferred to G8's combinators, arity reserved.
# Members compare by CANONICAL FORM, which reduces to scalar identity
# for scalars (unique-leafwise above) and gives structural equality for
# CONTAINER members without a second rule. Review caught that "scalar
# identity" alone left these undefined, which would have let the two
# ports pick different comparisons -- object identity in one, canon or
# len counts what GENERATES. An optional key that never resolves is
# dropped at generation and does not count, so the first row HOLDS.
# An optional key SURVIVES unification carrying its unresolved value
# only in BagVal.gen -- nothing in the fixpoint settles it earlier. So a
# map holding one has no knowable count until generation, and len over
# such a map is COMPLETED AT GENERATION. A supplied optional DOES count.
# (The first draft of this said len "residuates until the optional
# resolves or is dropped"; review pointed out that drop never happens
# during unification, so the atom would be stuck forever.)
